rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord must not terminate a tenancy without just cause. Just cause includes at-fault reasons (such as non-payment of rent, lease violations, nuisance, waste, criminal activity, or unlawful use) and no-fault reasons (owner or family occupation, withdrawal from rental market, compliance with government orders or habitability requirements, or demolition or substantial remodeling). For leases entered into after June 24, 2023, owner-occupation terminations require tenant agreement or an express lease provision allowing unilateral termination.
rules.quotedSpan: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.coverageDescription: Applies to residential rental properties in San Diego, except: transient/tourist hotels, short-term rentals, deed-restricted affordable housing, subsidized affordable housing (excluding Section 8), mobilehomes under state law, non-profit hospitals/facilities, dormitories, properties where tenant shares kitchen/bath with owner-occupant landlord, single-family residences with owner-occupant and no more than two bedrooms or ADUs, two-unit properties with owner-occupant, properties with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years (unless mobilehome), and certain small owner-occupied properties meeting specific criteria.
exemptions: Properties issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless mobilehome)
Single-family residence with landlord principal residence (max two bedrooms, two ADUs, or two JADUs)
Two-unit building with owner-occupant continuing in occupancy
Small owner-operated properties without corporate/REIT/LLC-with-corporate ownership that provide required notice
Non-profit hospital, religious facility, extended care facility, or non-profit transitional housing
Properties where tenant shares kitchen or bathroom with owner-occupant
Mobilehomes subject to state Mobilehome Residency Law

rules.title: Notice and Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Terminations
rules.requirement: For no-fault just cause terminations (owner/family occupation, withdrawal from market, compliance with government orders, or demolition/substantial remodeling), the landlord must provide written notice at least 30 or 60 days in advance (as required by California law) describing the basis, stating the tenant's right to relocation assistance, and informing tenants of their right to receive an offer to renew if the property is re-rented for residential purposes within five years. Relocation assistance is two months of actual rent (or three months if tenant is senior or disabled), provided by direct payment or rent waiver, and must be delivered within 15 days of notice if by direct payment.
rules.quotedSpan: The landlord shall, regardless of the tenant's income or length of tenancy and at the landlord's option, provide relocation assistance to the tenant by one of the following: (A) The landlord shall provide a direct payment to the tenant. (i) Unless section 98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii) applies, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to two months of actual rent under the tenant's lease in effect at the date of the notice. (ii) If the tenant is a senior or disabled, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to three months of actual rent
rules.coverageDescription: Same as just cause rule above; applies to residential rental properties subject to §98.0704 terminations for no-fault just cause.
